scores.evidence: Every view opens with a one-line question title ('How does offstage execute a command away from your screen?', 'How does a fleet box claim a task, run it in a slot, and wipe it?', etc.), an audience line ('Engineers onboarding to offstage and offstage cloud') and a scope sentence that says what is left to sibling views. The level of detail (routes, timeouts, uids) suits that audience. The one blemish is the app header, which shows a random canvas id ('vp-offstage-detailed-SCyg6I') instead of a set title.

View 1 is a context view and views 2–7 are zoom-ins, and the boxes are mostly at component level. Two things are stray. View 2 draws 'Headless lane' and 'Xvfb container lane' as peer participants of 'Session lane: sessiond', but the first two are code running inside the CLI process (view 3's subtitle admits this for the session client), while sessiond is a separate daemon in another account. The router, which is the component offstage exists for, is folded into the CLI box text ('Routes local lanes'). Sessiond is a box in view 2 but only an arrow-label word ('sessiond op') in views 5 and 6.

Views are tightly scoped, and the omissions are stated ('result persistence is in the next view', 'helper display is covered in the local execution view'). Unstated gaps: (1) view 2 never shows what sends a command to which lane (no --headed, xcodebuild, simctl or open -a triggers), and the refusal exists only as note text; (2) view 1's notes say 'the CLI also offers sandbox tools', but the CLI is not drawn there, although view 4 draws it as a cloud client; (3) view 7 mentions billing and email verification, but no billing or mail provider appears anywhere (the code uses Stripe and api.resend.com).

Every arrow I could see is labelled with protocol, payload and response, plus sync or local: 'B2 HTTPS long-poll /claim ≤25 s → work or 204 (sync)', 'C4 HTTPS /v1/model/messages with run token (sync)'. The legend fixes one meaning (caller → recipient, response included). Step numbers A1–A3, B1–B5, C1–C6 and D1–D4 give an order across views. Minor problems: in view 4, B1 sits below both C1 arrows in a top-down timeline, which implies an order that doesn't exist; and the 'B3/C3' and 'B5/C6' shared-step codes take decoding.

Views 2–7 draw labelled containers that state ownership and deployment: 'Self-hosted Mac', 'Fly-managed: one machine (sjc) + offstage_data volume', 'Managed external providers; outside offstage trust boundary', 'Same Studio A Mac; separate customer uids'. Deductions: view 1, the overview, has no containers at all, only subtitle tags under each box. 'Fleet Mac: operator uid' and 'Fleet Mac: slot uids' are side-by-side siblings with no enclosing Studio A machine boundary. The same goes for the three regions on the developer's Mac ('Same machine' is text only). The network boundary (tailnet, pf LAN guard) appears only in notes. Containers and components are both pale or bold versions of the same red.

No edge crosses another edge in any view. Each view has one direction: left to right in view 1, top-down timelines in views 2–7. Spacing is even and text is readable at 1194×834. Deductions: the notes panel takes about 195 of 834 px (y≈560–755), so the drawing gets a band about 400 px tall. Views 5 and 6 shrink to roughly 11 px box text while leaving about 150 px of empty margin at the right. Lifelines stop abruptly at the panel. Arrow labels run across intermediate lifelines (view 4 C1 across the CLI line at x≈495, view 6 C4 and C5 across the runner line at x≈515, view 7 D1 across the plane line). In view 1, Fleet runner sits in the left column with the customer clients, so it reads as one more customer rather than the execution side. Selector titles are cut off ('1/7 · How do cloud clients reach fleet …').

There is a legend on every view: caller → recipient, headers = boundaries, faint guides = actors, cylinders = stores, solid = sync request, dotted = local I/O, equal stages = alternatives, unnumbered = independent. Line style and shape apply it consistently, which gives signals that don't depend on colour (cylinders for Run directory and Fly volume, dotted lines for local I/O). Deductions: the legend is generic (view 1 lists headers, guides and cylinders it doesn't contain). The flow letters (A = local, B = task, C = sandbox/agent, D = console) are never in the legend; each is defined only in its own view's subtitle, so view 5's 'B2–B5 … C3/C6' is opaque if you arrive from the selector. 'External' is signalled by text alone. Single-colour red ink flattens the hierarchy.

Failure behaviour is explicit, with source paths given: the Fly plane on one machine as a single point of failure; acked writes held in memory with a snapshot every 2 s plus on SIGTERM, so a crash can lose about 2 s; claim long-poll ≤25 s returning 204; unstarted 20 s → requeue, max 3 tries; a box silent for 2 min fails its running task without rerunning it; heartbeat every 15 s delivers cancels; '409 = cancelled'; the LAN guard fails closed; reset before the next claim; no fallback to your display ('exit 69'); refusal on every lane; result.json writes can fail; op answers resent with backoff; the API key stays on the plane, with model, step and max_tokens checks. It is nearly all in the notes text rather than marked on the drawn components, and capacity (one Studio, offstage0–7) is only implied.

Each view has a footer: 'Source review 2026-11-05 · 57eeabc + local edits · Owner: Viaat Das (package.json author) · Live runtime NOT verified'. I spot-checked about 20 names and numbers against the code and they match: MAX_POLL_MS 25_000, CLAIM_ACK_MS 20_000, MAX_ATTEMPTS 3, BOX_LOST_MS 2 min, HEARTBEAT_MS 15_000, plane.json every 2 s plus SIGTERM, omt_ tokens, x-anthropic-api-key, /v1/model/messages, /v1/auth/clerk, Clerk JWKS, exit 69, DISPLAY dropped, --rm, fluxbox, stdin ignored, sudo -n -u. Capped at 3 because no runtime check was done.

A newcomer can correctly retell the cloud path (SDK or console → Fly plane; the Studio runner long-polls, runs work as slot uids and resets them; agent model calls go through the plane to Anthropic) and the local path (CLI picks headless, Xvfb container or helper-session lane; artifacts go to a per-run directory). They cannot learn which commands go to which lane, how local offstage relates to the fleet (both use sessiond), or what billing and email depend on. Reading seven views plus dense notes, and decoding B3/C3, takes longer than two minutes. View 1's layout invites the misreading that the fleet is another client.

visualVerdict: Good, 33/40, and not messy at the level of a single view. Each of the seven views is sparse, has a clear direction, has no edge crossing another edge, labels every arrow with protocol, payload and sync/local, and carries a title question, a legend and a dated provenance footer. The 'messy and unusable' feeling most likely comes from the set, not from any one drawing. Everything is the same red ink, so there is little visual hierarchy. A dense notes-and-legend panel takes about a quarter of the screen and pushes views 5–6 down to small text. Step codes like 'B3/C3' and 'Equal stages = alternatives' have to be decoded. And the entry view is weak: no boundaries, and the fleet placed among the customers. The biggest content gap is that the local-execution view never shows how offstage decides which lane a command goes to.
coldRead: What a new engineer can learn from these screens: offstage has a local half and a cloud half. Locally, the 'offstage CLI / MCP' running in your Mac account sends a command to exactly one of three lanes. Headless runs it in place with execa. The Xvfb container lane runs it under docker run --rm with the repo read-only and the host DISPLAY dropped. The session lane hands it over a unix socket to sessiond in a separate 'computeruse' account with its own window server, which can also take screenshots and inject input. Logs and screen.png land in a per-run directory, and the CLI writes result.json for every verdict, refusals included. With no substrate the run is skipped (exit 69) and never falls back to your screen. Installers, .pkg/.dmg and hdiutil are refused on every lane. In the cloud, customers use the SDK or web console (and the CLI's sandbox tools) to call a single Fly.io machine, 'offstage-api'. It authenticates and checks the GUI gate, capacity and credit, queues work fairly, keeps state in memory, and snapshots it to /data every 2 s. A fleet runner on Studio A, running as the operator account, long-polls /claim. It runs work as offstage0–7 slot accounts via sessiond or sudo -n -u, reports events and artifacts back, heartbeats every 15 s for cancels, and resets each slot (kill, wipe, new uid) before the next claim. Agent runs reach Claude through the plane, so the slot only ever holds an omt_ run token, never the customer's key. Console sign-in can go through Clerk, and the token is exchanged for a plane session. What they cannot tell: (1) which commands go to which local lane, since view 2 shows three A1 alternatives with no rule; (2) that the fleet's slots reuse the same sessiond as the local session lane, which appears only as the word 'sessiond' in a label; (3) whether a slot is GUI or headless and when each is used; (4) what external services billing and email verification depend on; (5) whether the two Studio boundaries are one machine; this has to be inferred from 'Same Studio A Mac' text; (6) the network path between Studio and Fly (tailnet, pf guard), mentioned only in notes. Uncertain from the image alone: whether 'Fleet runner' in view 1 is a customer-side actor (its placement suggests so, but the label says 'Fleet Mac: operator uid'), and whether the C1 arrows in view 4 happen before or after B1.
mostSeriousProblems: View 2 ('How does offstage execute a command away from your screen?') omits the routing decision. Three 'A1' alternative arrows go to headless, container and session with no visible rule for choosing between them (no --headed/headless:false → container, no xcodebuild/simctl/open -a/osascript → session), and the refusal path exists only as note text. That decision is the core of what offstage does.

View 1, the entry and context view, is the weakest. It draws no boundaries (only subtitle tags). It puts 'Fleet runner' in the left column with the customer clients, so it reads as one more customer instead of the execution side. It leaves out the CLI as a cloud client even though its own note says the CLI offers sandbox tools and view 4 draws it. The set has no single picture that ties local offstage, the plane, the fleet and the external dependencies together.

Single-colour red for every container, component, arrow and label flattens the hierarchy. Boundaries differ from components only by a paler stroke, and external services ('Anthropic Messages API (external)', 'Clerk social sign-in (external)') differ only by text.

The notes-and-legend panel (y≈560–755) takes about 23% of the 834 px height on every view. The drawing gets about 400 px, so views 5 and 6 shrink to about 11 px box text while leaving wide empty margins, and lifelines end abruptly against the panel.

Step notation is cryptic and not defined consistently. The A/B/C/D flow letters are defined only in individual subtitles. 'B3/C3' and 'B5/C6' (shared steps) and 'Equal stages = alternatives' must be decoded. In view 4, B1 is drawn below both C1 arrows in a top-down timeline, which implies a false order.
Arrow labels run across intermediate lifelines: view 4 C1 across the CLI line, view 6 C4 and C5 across the Fleet runner line, view 7 D1 across the plane line.

Missing boundaries and dependencies. There is no enclosing 'Studio A Mac' around the operator and slot regions, and no enclosing 'your Mac' around the developer account, Docker container and helper session. No network boundary (tailnet, pf LAN guard) is drawn. Billing (Stripe) and email verification (Resend) appear nowhere, although view 7 cites billing and verification.
recommendations: Rebuild view 1 as a true system overview. Draw boundary boxes for: customer side (SDK, web console, CLI sandbox tools); Fly offstage-api (plane + /data); Studio A fleet box (operator runner + offstage0–7 slots), drawn to the right of the plane so work visibly flows outward; your Mac (CLI/MCP and the three local lanes); and third parties (Anthropic, Clerk, Stripe, Resend). Each region should point to its detail view.

Add the routing decision to view 2. Draw a router/decision node with the trigger per lane (default → headless; --headed, headless:false or GPU flags → container; xcodebuild, simctl, XCUITest, open -a or osascript → session) and a drawn 'refused' outcome for installer, .pkg/.dmg and hdiutil, instead of leaving it in the notes.

Give the drawing back its vertical space. Collapse the notes panel by default or shrink it to one line. Show only the legend entries each view actually uses. Scale views 5 and 6 to the full width so box text is at least 13 px.

Add a second visual channel for hierarchy: a distinct fill or dashed grey border for external services, a heavier enclosing frame for machine boundaries (Studio A, your Mac), and stronger contrast between boundaries and components. Keep the non-colour cues that already work.

Put the flow-letter key (A local run, B cloud task, C sandbox/agent, D console sign-in) in the legend of every view. Replace 'B3/C3' with a single 'shared step' marker, and order arrows truly top-down (in view 4, put B1 first or split B and C into separate bands).
Keep labels off lifelines: give labels a background halo, or offset them so they don't straddle the Fleet runner, CLI and plane lines in views 4, 6 and 7.

In the fleet views, draw the pf LAN guard and tailnet path as a network boundary between Studio A and Fly. Show sessiond as a component inside the slot region so the link to the local session lane is visible.
Show the full view titles in the selector, or shorten them so they fit, and give the canvas a human-readable set title instead of 'vp-offstage-detailed-SCyg6I'.
